messages:
Maya: hey all — starting week 1, quick setup qs about keys + network. Where do I get a hosted API key vs the sandbox key my onboarding email mentioned? Also our corp firewall needs IPs to allowlist — does Redwood publish stable egress IPs for the hosted API? And last: what are the default quotas/rate limits for hosted keys (esp. streaming) so I don't accidentally flood things.

OnboardBot: Welcome to Redwood, Maya! :tada: You should have received a sandbox key in your onboarding email (short-lived). Hosted API keys live in Console → Settings → API Keys once your account is provisioned. See: https://intranet.redwood.example.com/onboarding/keys (internal).

Sam: tl;dr — hosted keys = long-lived & intended for dev/prod, sandbox = test only (low quota). For most new hires sandbox is enough for tutorials. If you need a hosted key now ping your manager or @sam and we can create one for you.

Maya: thanks — is there a quick note on rotating keys? we use a CI service that needs a stable token or rotation process.

Sam: Recommended flow: create a new hosted key in the Console, deploy it to your env (e.g., CI secret), then revoke the old one after verification. No special downtime; the service accepts either key while you swap. We normally rotate every quarter.

Eli: on the networking piece — we do publish a list of gateway IP ranges for the hosted API but they can change (CDN, infra moves). Internal doc here: https://intranet.redwood.example.com/networking/egress-ips (subscribe for updates). If your firewall team requires low churn, ask infra for a dedicated egress NAT or consider Redwood Dedicated/Private which has stable IPs. Also allowing by DNS/hostname (e.g., outbound to api.redwood.example.com) is usually more robust than fixed IPs.

Maya: ok makes sense. any hard numbers for default rate limits / tokens/day? streaming behaviour?

Sam: Defaults vary by org type but typical starter limits: ~20 requests/sec (per-api-key soft limit) and 100k tokens/day for hosted developer accounts. Streams count against token quotas similarly. If you hit rate limits you get 429s with headers: 

  x-rate-limit-limit: 20
  x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
  Retry-After: 12

Follow these patterns: exponential backoff with jitter, respect Retry-After, and avoid busy-waiting. Example (bash):

  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \ 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
    -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","input":"hi"}' \ 
    https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate

If you see persistent streaming 429s, either reduce concurrency/batch size or request a quota uplift. For production streaming apps we recommend Dedicated (predictable throughput) or shard across keys with careful rate limiting.

Priya: security note — do not commit keys to repos. Use our Vault path: secret/onboarding/new-hires/<your-username> for the sandbox key and secret/teams/<team>/redwood for hosted keys. If you need an allowlist ticket for our IP ranges, tag me @Priya and infra will open a request with the network team.

Maya: awesome — this helps a lot. I'll try the sandbox flows first and ping @Sam if we need a hosted key. One last Q: are there token cost differences between sandbox and hosted?

Sam: sandbox is functionally same models but sometimes throttled or behind lower quotas; billing differs (sandbox free credits vs billed hosted usage). Costs per-token are the same for the model family, but sandbox usage won't show up on invoices.

Maya: perfect, thanks everyone! :pray:

Eli: ping here if you want help setting up CI secrets or load testing. Happy to pair for 10–15m later today. :coffee:
